## What this letter says
You came to hospital after taking too much paracetamol (an overdose). You had treatment through a drip (acetylcysteine). Your liver blood tests are now normal. You saw the liaison psychiatry team on 21 September 2026. The Crisis Team will visit you at home.

## What you need to do
1. Be at home on 23 September 2026. The Crisis Team will visit you there.

## Dates and medicines
- 20 September 2026: you were admitted to hospital.
- 21 September 2026: you saw the liaison psychiatry team.
- 22 September 2026: you were discharged from hospital.
- 23 September 2026: the Crisis Team will visit you at home.
- Medicines: the letter lists no medicines to take at home.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What is acetylcysteine?
- What does the liaison psychiatry team do?
- What will the Crisis Team do when they visit me?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
